#### What this PR does / why we need it:
ClusterQueue treated `nil` as `0` by defaulting the float and only filling it when the field was non-nil.
Thus `kueue_cluster_queue_borrowing_limit` misreported “unlimited” as `0`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Relates to #11835

  * Improved quota reporting test coverage with table-driven test approach.

## Walkthrough

This PR explicitly defines and reports cluster queue borrowing limits as positive infinity when unset. The core logic change in the scheduler's `reportResourceMetrics` function is paired with updated metric definition text, refactored validation tests, and clarified user-facing documentation.

## Changes

**Borrowing Limit Infinity Reporting**

| Layer / File(s) | Summary |
|---|---|
| **Borrowing limit infinity reporting implementation** <br> `pkg/cache/scheduler/clusterqueue.go` | When a resource quota has no `BorrowingLimit` (`nil`), `reportResourceMetrics` now explicitly reports the borrowing limit as `math.Inf(1)` instead of leaving it unset. |
| **Metric definition and validation tests** <br> `pkg/metrics/metrics.go`, `pkg/metrics/metrics_test.go` | The `ClusterQueueResourceBorrowingLimit` gauge help text is updated to document `+Inf` behavior. Test file imports `math` and refactors `TestReportAndCleanupClusterQueueQuotas` into a table-driven approach with dynamic metric count assertions. |
| **User-facing documentation update** <br> `site/content/en/docs/reference/metrics.md` | The `kueue_cluster_queue_borrowing_limit` metric description now explicitly states that unset borrowing limits report as `+Inf`. |

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 2 (Simple) | ⏱️ ~12 minutes

## Poem

> A limit unbounded, now clear as can be,  
> When nil becomes ∞ in metrics we see,  
> The tests are refactored with table-driven grace,  
> And docs paint infinity's elegant face. 🐇✨
